comparisons.peer_summary: Citi faces losses from defaults by other clearing members and market-wide disruptions due to the interconnectedness of financial institutions, such as regional bank failures.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Citigroup (C) disclose credit risk exposure stemming from their membership in central clearing counterparties (CCPs). BAC explicitly states it is 'a member of various CCPs' and faces exposure if a member defaults, potentially requiring it to pay a portion of losses. Similarly, Citi notes it is 'also a member of various central clearing counterparties' and could incur financial losses due to requirements for clearing members to share losses resulting from defaults by other members. Both disclosures highlight the specific risk of loss-sharing obligations within the CCP structure.

sentences.text: We are also a member of various CCPs, which results in credit risk exposure to those CCPs.
In the event that one or more members of a CCP defaults on their obligations, we may be required to pay a portion of any losses incurred by such CCP.

Citi is also a member of various central clearing counterparties and could incur financial losses as a result of defaults by other clearing members due to the requirements of clearing members to share losses.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces risks from third-party defaults due to bankruptcy, lack of liquidity, or operational failure, which could adversely affect profitability and liquidity. Additionally, the failure of significant market participants or institutions could lead to contagion, causing significant liquidity problems, losses, or defaults by other institutions, and the company may be exposed to special assessments under the FDIA or OLA.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Goldman Sachs (GS) disclose risks associated with the failure or default of significant market participants. BAC specifically warns that 'default by a significant market participant may result in further risk and potential losses.' GS similarly notes that 'A failure of a significant market participant... could in the future lead to significant liquidity problems, losses or defaults by other institutions, which in turn could adversely affect us.' While BAC links this generally to risk exposure, GS provides more detail on the contagion effect (losses by other institutions) and mentions exposure to special assessments under FDIA or OLA, whereas BAC does not mention regulatory assessments in this specific context.

sentences.text: Also, default by a significant market participant may result in further risk and potential losses.

A failure of a significant market participant, or even concerns about a default by such an institution, has in the past and could in the future lead to significant liquidity problems, losses or defaults by other institutions, which in turn could adversely affect us.

We are also exposed to the risk of a special assessment, including under the FDIA or OLA in the event of the failure of a bank or non-bank financial institution, which have in the past, and may in the future, adversely affect our results of operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: A central counterparty (CCP) failure requires replacing contracts, increasing costs and potential losses; the firm may also bear its share of member defaults or non-default losses from CCP activities like custodial or cyber breaches.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and JPMorgan (JPM) identify the risk of bearing a share of losses if a member of a Central Counterparty (CCP) defaults. BAC states, 'In the event that one or more members of a CCP defaults on their obligations, we may be required to pay a portion of any losses incurred by such CCP.' JPMorgan mirrors this with, 'JPMorganChase can be exposed to losses if a member of a CCP... defaults on its obligations... because of requirements that each member of the CCP absorb a portion of those losses.' Both disclosures focus on the structural obligation of clearing members to absorb losses from peers, though JPMorgan also expands the topic to include non-default losses (e.g., cyber breaches) which BAC does not mention in this specific disclosure.

sentences.text: In the event that one or more members of a CCP defaults on their obligations, we may be required to pay a portion of any losses incurred by such CCP.

In addition, JPMorganChase can be exposed to losses if a member of a CCP in which JPMorganChase is also a member defaults on its obligations to the CCP because of requirements that each member of the CCP absorb a portion of those losses.

comparisons.peer_summary: As a clearing member, the company is responsible for customer defaults or misconduct and may incur financial losses, which may arise from events difficult to detect or foresee.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America (BAC) and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose financial loss risk as a clearing member due to defaults by other clearing members. BAC explains, 'In the event that one or more members of a CCP defaults on their obligations, we may be required to pay a portion of any losses incurred by such CCP.' MS states, 'we are responsible for the defaults or misconduct of our customers and could incur financial losses in the event of default by other clearing members.' Both entities explicitly link their status as clearing members to the liability for peer defaults.

sentences.text: In the event that one or more members of a CCP defaults on their obligations, we may be required to pay a portion of any losses incurred by such CCP.

In addition, as a clearing member of several central counterparties, we are responsible for the defaults or misconduct of our customers and could incur financial losses in the event of default by other clearing members.
